statement: Define a word of report[i] to be a maximal contiguous run of non-space bytes. For each student ID s = student_id[i], define points(s) = 3 * (number of words of report[i] that are byte-equal to some element of positive_feedback) - (number of words of report[i] that are byte-equal to some element of negative_feedback); this is well-defined because the student_id values are pairwise distinct. Say that a student ID s outranks a student ID t iff points(s) > points(t), or points(s) = points(t) and s < t. Whenever top_students returns a result r, all of the following hold: (1) len(r) = k; (2) every entry r[j] equals student_id[i] for some i with 0 <= i < n; (3) the entries r[0..k-1] are pairwise distinct; (4) for all 0 <= a < b < k, r[a] outranks r[b]; (5) for every 0 <= a < k and every student ID s that occurs among student_id[0..n-1] but does not occur among r[0..k-1], r[a] outranks s. These conditions uniquely determine r: it is exactly the sequence of the k highest-ranked students, ordered by non-increasing points with ties broken by smaller student ID.
preconditions: Let n = len(report) = len(student_id). Constraints: 1 <= n <= 10^4; 1 <= len(positive_feedback) and 1 <= len(negative_feedback); every word in positive_feedback and negative_feedback is a non-empty byte string of lowercase ASCII letters of length <= 100; no byte string occurs in both positive_feedback and negative_feedback; every report[i] is a non-empty byte string of lowercase letters and spaces of length <= 100, with exactly one space between consecutive words and no leading or trailing space; every student_id[i] satisfies 1 <= student_id[i] <= 10^9; the values student_id[0..n-1] are pairwise distinct; 1 <= k <= n.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, top_students returns a result r and does not fail: no 64-bit integer overflow, no out-of-bounds indexing or slicing, and no panic occur.

preconditions: Same as spec_1, with 1 <= k <= k' <= n.
